Teacher Resume Example: Write a Teaching Resume That Passes the ATS in 2026

Teaching resumes face a double gate: the district's hiring system and a principal who skims each application in seconds. Generic duty lists — "prepared lesson plans," "managed classroom" — fail at both. Screening software ranks you low on keyword match, and the principal sees no evidence of what your students actually achieved.

What gets shortlisted is proof: a valid teaching credential up front, named certifications and endorsements, grade levels and class sizes described precisely, the learning platforms you run (Google Classroom, Canvas), and outcomes with numbers. Below: a complete annotated example, plus the ATS rules for teaching hiring.

Quick answer: A teacher resume should include: a valid state teaching credential with subject endorsements, named certifications (e.g., ESL, special education), grade levels and class sizes taught, measurable student outcomes (test-score gains, pass rates), classroom technology (Google Classroom, Canvas), and keywords mirrored from the posting. District screening systems check credentials first — duty lists without numbers get ranked down.

Key Takeaways

  • Lead with your credential — state teaching certificate, subject endorsements, expiry status. District filters check these before reading anything else.
  • Name your teaching environment precisely: grade level, subject, class size (e.g., 28-student 7th-grade ELA), school type.
  • Quantify student outcomes: test-score gains, pass-rate improvements, attendance, intervention results.
  • Mirror the posting's exact terms — "differentiated instruction," "IEP," and "PLC" are distinct ATS keywords.
  • Keep formatting ATS-clean: single column, standard headings, no graphics, no text boxes, no creative section titles.

Teacher Resume Example (Annotated)

YOUR NAME
City, ST | (555) 555-0100 | youremail@email.com
linkedin.com/in/yourname

CERTIFICATION
Professional Teaching Certificate — [State], active (expires 2028)
Endorsements: English Language Arts (6–12), English as a Second Language (ESL)

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Middle-school ELA teacher with 6 years across grades 6–8, leading 25–30 student classes. Raised state reading proficiency 18 percentage points over three years through data-driven small-group intervention. Google Classroom and Canvas lead teacher; mentor for 4 new hires.

Why it works: years, grade band, class sizes, one outcome metric, platforms named literally, mentoring leadership — every claim verifiable.

TEACHING EXPERIENCE

ELA Teacher — Grades 7–8 | Lincoln Middle School | 2021 – Present
• Lead 28-student ELA classes; raised state reading proficiency from 54% to 72% over three years
• Built data-driven small-group intervention using i-Ready diagnostics; struggling readers gained an average of 1.5 grade levels per year
• Co-chair the ELA professional learning community (PLC); designed common assessments used across 6 grade-level teams
• Mentor 4 new teachers through first-year induction; all retained past year two

Why it works: class size, named diagnostic, measured gains, PLC leadership, mentoring — the same proof-over-adjectives principle in our customer service resume example.

Student Teacher — Grade 5 | [Elementary School] | 2019 – 2021
• Completed 14-week full-time student teaching in a 26-student 5th-grade classroom; taught full persuasive-writing unit with Google Classroom assignments
• Raised unit assessment average from 71% to 84% using differentiated stations for three reading levels
• Co-led parent-teacher conferences for 24 families with cooperating teacher

EDUCATION

Bachelor of Arts in English Education — [University] | 2019
[State] Teaching Credential Program, Professional Certificate

TEACHING SKILLS

Google Classroom, Canvas | i-Ready, NWEA MAP | differentiated instruction | IEP/504 collaboration | PBIS | formative assessment | parent communication

What Schools and Hiring Software Scan For

The Jobscan 2026 ATS Usage Report puts ATS usage at 97.4% of Fortune 500 companies — and school districts screen through similar systems (Frontline, AppliTrack), since one teaching posting can draw hundreds of applicants. The software filters before any human reads your resume, scoring on exact credential and keyword matches.

Here's what both the software and the principal look for, in priority order:

  1. Credential and endorsements. Active state certificate, subject endorsements, ESL or special education add-ons. If the posting requires an ESL endorsement and your resume never says "ESL," you can be filtered out regardless of experience.
  2. Teaching context. Grade level, subject, class size, school type. "28-student 7th-grade ELA" says what you've handled; "taught middle school" says nothing.
  3. Platforms and tools. Google Classroom, Canvas, i-Ready, NWEA MAP — districts search these terms literally. Differentiated instruction, IEP/504 collaboration, PBIS.
  4. Outcomes with numbers. Test-score gains, pass-rate improvements, attendance, intervention results — the same proof-over-adjectives principle in our nursing resume example.
  5. Keywords from the posting. Mirror exact terms. If the posting says "professional learning community," write "professional learning community," not just "team meetings." The parser matches text, not intent.

New Teacher vs. Experienced Teacher Resume Structure

New teachers

  • Lead with certification and student teaching: state certificate, endorsements, then placements — grade level, class size, subjects taught, one measured result per placement. Example: "7th-grade ELA student teaching, 14 weeks — 26 students; full persuasive-writing unit, Google Classroom assignments."
  • Endorsements carry extra weight. ESL or special education add-ons before you apply stand out in crowded applicant pools.
  • Translate adjacent experience. Tutoring, camp counseling, coaching, or paraprofessional work counts — quantify it. See our guide to writing a resume with no experience.

Experienced teachers (3+ years)

  • Lead with a 3-line summary (years, grade band, class sizes, one metric), then reverse-chronological teaching experience.
  • Condense student teaching to one line under education, or drop it after 5+ years.
  • Show progression: PLC leadership, mentoring, curriculum design, data-team work, committee roles.
  • Changing grade levels or subjects? Front-load transferable skills (differentiation, data-driven intervention, IEP collaboration) in the summary so the screener sees the bridge.

The Exact Sections of a Teacher Resume

1. Certification

Always first for teaching. Format: certificate type, state, status, expiry. Add endorsements with grade bands — "English Language Arts (6–12), ESL." Never list an expired certificate as current.

2. Professional Summary (3 lines max)

Years + grade band + class sizes + one metric + target. New teachers: lead with certification instead (e.g., "Newly certified ELA teacher (6–12) with ESL endorsement; 14 weeks of 7th-grade student teaching, 26-student classes.").

3. Teaching Experience

Reverse-chronological: title, grade level/subject, school, dates. Every bullet should carry at least one of: class size, a specific strategy or tool, or a measured outcome. "Responsible for lesson planning" gets ignored; "Designed 28-student ELA units in Google Classroom; raised unit average from 71% to 84%" gets interviews.

4. Education

Degree, school, graduation year. New teachers can add honors and relevant coursework; experienced teachers keep it to one line.

5. Teaching Skills

A scannable list for the keyword scan — name things literally: platforms (Google Classroom, Canvas), assessments (i-Ready, NWEA MAP), strategies (differentiated instruction, PBIS, formative assessment). Our teacher resume guide has more role-specific keyword lists.

ATS Formatting Rules for Teacher Resumes

  • Single column, always. Two-column templates scramble parsing order — your certification can end up attributed to the wrong section. Pick a single-column ATS-friendly template.
  • Standard headings: Summary, Certification, Teaching Experience, Education, Teaching Skills. "My Classroom Journey" is invisible to the parser.
  • No tables, text boxes, or graphics. Skill bars, icons, and text boxes are dropped or misread by most parsers. Plain text only.
  • Contact info in the body, not the header/footer. Many parsers skip headers and footers — if your phone number lives there, it may never be extracted.
  • Standard fonts, 10–12pt. Arial, Calibri, Georgia, Times New Roman.
  • File type: PDF unless the posting asks for .docx. Never Pages, image, or scanned files.
  • Length: one page for new teachers; two pages max for experienced teachers. Cut oldest roles first, not the metrics.
  • Verify before you apply: run your resume through Cvyon's free ATS grader against the actual posting to catch parsing errors and keyword gaps.

7 Mistakes Teachers Make on Resumes

  1. Burying the certification below the fold. District filters check credentials first. On page two, they may never be read.
  2. Duty lists with no class sizes or outcomes. "Taught English" matches nothing. "28-student 7th-grade ELA; raised proficiency 54% to 72%" matches the posting's requirements.
  3. Abbreviations without expansion. Write "Individualized Education Program (IEP)" and "Professional Learning Community (PLC)" at least once — some systems index the full term, others the abbreviation.
  4. Creative section headings. "My Teaching Journey" and "Where I've Inspired" don't map to the parser's expected sections. Use the standard five.
  5. Two-column "modern" templates. They look sharp and parse terribly — content order scrambles, and certifications can vanish from the extracted text.
  6. Missing the posting's exact endorsement term. The posting says "English as a Second Language" and you only wrote "ESL" — keyword score drops. Mirror their words.
  7. Stale certifications. Listing a certificate with a 2024 expiry as current reads as careless. Update the resume the day you recertify.

Frequently Asked Questions

What should be included in a teacher resume?

A valid state teaching credential with subject endorsements; named certifications (e.g., ESL, special education); a summary with years, grade levels, and class sizes; teaching experience with student outcomes and named platforms (Google Classroom, Canvas); education; and a skills section with instructional strategies (differentiated instruction, IEP collaboration, PBIS). Every bullet should carry a number — class sizes, volumes, or outcome metrics.

How do I write a teacher resume with no experience?

Lead with your credential and a Student Teaching section: grade level, class size, and what you taught per placement (e.g., "7th-grade ELA student teaching, 14 weeks — 26 students; taught full unit on persuasive writing, Google Classroom assignments"). Add endorsements, and translate tutoring, camp counseling, or coaching work into quantified bullets. Schools hire new teachers on credentials and classroom exposure, not job titles.

What certifications should a teacher put on a resume?

Your state teaching certificate with subject endorsements and expiry status, plus add-ons matching your target: ESL/ELL, special education, gifted and talented, or AP. List the issuing state or body and keep only current credentials — an expired certificate presented as active damages credibility.

How long should a teacher resume be?

One page for new teachers and teachers under 5 years' experience; two pages maximum for experienced teachers. When trimming, cut older roles and redundant bullets — never the certification section, endorsements, or your strongest student-outcome metrics.

Should teachers include student teaching on a resume?

Yes, if you have under 3 years of full-time experience — treat it as a real placement with grade level, class size, subjects taught, and one measured result (e.g., "raised unit assessment average from 71% to 84%"). After 3+ years of full-time teaching, condense it to one line under education or drop it.

Do teacher resumes need to be ATS-friendly?

Yes — school districts receive hundreds of applications per posting, so screening through systems like Frontline and AppliTrack is standard in teaching hiring. Use a single-column layout, standard headings, credentials first, exact certification names, and keywords mirrored from the posting. Verify with Cvyon's free ATS grader before you apply.
